title: Airphoto Selection Pipeline
text: fly_footprint() converts point centroids rectangular polygons representing estimated ground coverage. standard 9” x 9” (228 mm) negative used BC aerial survey cameras produces footprint width 9 * scale * 0.0254 metres, default (negative_size = 9). Ground width scales recording format, figure film measurement. catalogue mixes film digital one layer — sampled area roughly fifth frames Digital - Colour — digital frame negative. fly_footprint() therefore sizes row media value records outcome footprint_basis. Frames whose format resolve get empty geometry rather plausible rectangle, every downstream function reports many excluded: Digital frames resolve "unknown_format" sensor width need centroid metadata. Supply know camera: fly_footprint(photos, format_size = c("Digital - Colour" = 3.54)). photos used throughout vignette 1968 film, every footprint sized 9-inch negative. Note footprints assume flat terrain beneath aircraft. slopes true ground coverage differs — downhill slopes produce larger actual footprint, uphill slopes smaller one. coverage overlap numbers downstream inherit approximation. Figure @ref(fig:fig-footprint) shows estimated footprints 20 photos. Notice centroids fall outside AOI footprints still overlap — fly_filter() method = "footprint" catches edge cases simple centroid--polygon filter miss. Estimated photo footprints (blue rectangles) centroids (red dots) overlaid Upper Bulkley River floodplain AOI. Comparison spatial filtering methods.
